model.whole_body_acceleration: a_i,K = kappa_F H_i [omega_i x G_phase V_i,CMB]

coupling_derivation.interpretation: Required coupling under the Earth-only attribution that the K-indexed component of the fitted Earth eccentricity-vector and apsidal motion is generated by the K-Field term.

figures.caption: The origin-locked Cell3 primitive cell in two equal-scale ICRS views. All 27 centered half-step nodes are labelled by integer index, the six boundary faces are shown, and basis vectors a, b, and c originate at O=(0,0,0).

Six individual equal-scale Cell3 boundary faces. Every face contains the complete nine-node half-step array; labels preserve the full integer address and coordinates are derived from the exact ICRS basis.

Earth heliocentric trajectory for the 366-day calculation, with the projected Earth-Sun K vector and observed aphelion axis. The radial-alignment point and aphelion are separated by 2.5062 deg; maximum positive tangential K acceleration occurs approximately one quarter orbit earlier.

Daily Earth radial, tangential, and normal K-acceleration coefficients and the causal osculating semimajor-axis response. The integrated orbital-size response follows the tangential forcing by approximately 89.60 deg.

Observed one-year ICRS eccentricity-vector change from the fitted JPL Earth-Moon-barycenter element rates, compared with the unit K response scaled by the least-squares Earth coupling. The directional separation is 27.47 deg and the K-indexed projection contains 78.7% of the observed vector-rate power.
Two Earth-only calibrations: full eccentricity-vector projection and scalar apsidal-rate matching. Their 2.1% agreement defines the internal calibration interval 3.0e-11 to 3.1e-11.

Earth-Sun differential K acceleration through the one-year daily interval at the Earth-calibrated coupling. The total coefficient gives 5.68e-10 to 7.08e-10 m/s^2; the maximum tangential component is approximately 5.84e-10 m/s^2.
